//: Cases every Treebars SDK runs against its own implementation, shared so that the SDKs cannot disagree. Generated; do not edit.

scenarios.name: with nothing held and no version named, nothing is asked for and every read is the fallback
an upload's answer naming a version this install does not hold fetches once; the same version again does not
a key read in a session keeps that answer for the session; a key not yet read takes the newest
a key read as not set stays not set for the session, and takes its value in the next
a new session forgets what was read, and announces a change only when a read would now answer differently
activating applies the newest values to keys already read, and says whether anything changed
at sign-out what depended on the account is dropped at once and asked for again as nobody
at sign-in from nobody the answers are kept until the account's own arrive, and then replace what was read
signing in as somebody else drops the last account's answers at once
an account changes nothing when no answer depends on one: nothing is dropped and nothing is asked
attributes the app sets are sent with the next ask, and setting the same ones again asks nothing
with no variables held, attributes are kept for later and nothing is asked
while an ask is out nothing else starts one; if who is asking changed meanwhile, one more follows it
a refusal that names a wait keeps what is held and is not asked again before it
a failure that names no wait is asked again after the default one
a refused write key waits out the cooldown an upload's would
the wait survives a relaunch
what is held and what was read survive a relaunch inside the session, and a new session forgets the reads
a launch that describes the device differently from the last ask asks again; one that does not, does not
attributes survive a relaunch, so setting them again on every launch asks nothing
a read of the wrong kind answers the fallback, and never a value bent into shape
an override answers before anything held, is never kept, and never becomes what was read
the app can ask now: it answers whether a set arrived, joins an ask already out, and respects a wait
an answer that is not a config is a failure: what is held stays
the first read that answers an experiment's variant reports it, once: not the read after, nor a read no experiment decides
a new session inside a day reports nothing more, and a read a day later reports the same variant again
a read that does not answer the variant reports nothing: asked as another kind, listed, or answered by an override
what was reported is remembered across a launch: the same variant is not reported again inside the day
a different variant is reported at once, whatever the clock says
